```{=latex}
\quickfacts{OUTPUT}{One file (HTML / PDF / Word)}{STRUCTURE}{Single \texttt{.qmd}, no project needed}{BEST FOR}{Handouts, homework, printables}
```

## 1 — Setup

**Install (once per computer):**

- **VS Code** — [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com) (tick **"Add to PATH"** during setup)
- **Quarto CLI** — [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)
- **Quarto extension** for VS Code — search "Quarto" in the Extensions sidebar

::: {.callout-note}
## Only if you want PDF output
`quarto install tinytex` in the Terminal — installs the LaTeX engine Quarto needs for PDF. Skip this if you only want HTML or Word.
:::

**Create the file:** **File → New File… → Quarto Document** → save it as e.g. `exercises.qmd`. Unlike a website, this is a single file — no project folder structure needed.

```{=latex}
\begin{spotlight}{Which one do I need?}
Need one self-contained document to print, email, or hand out --- with a title, deadline, and export to PDF or Word? This is it. For a full multi-page site, see the \textbf{Website} cheatsheet; for a long document with numbered chapters, see the \textbf{Book} cheatsheet.
\end{spotlight}
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 2 — Writing your exercise sheet

**Page header** sets the title, author, and output format:

```yaml
---
title: "Exercise Sheet 1"
author: "Your Name"
format: pdf
---
```

**Body:** use `##` for each exercise, plain paragraphs for the text, `$...$` for inline math:

```markdown
## Exercise 1

Calculate the derivative of $f(x) = x^2 + 3x$.
```

**Code examples:** a plain fence just *displays* code without running it — good for "here's what the answer looks like":

```python
x = [1, 2, 3, 4]
print(sum(x))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Want it to actually run?
Tag the fence `{python}` instead of `python` — it executes via Jupyter and the output is embedded right in the PDF or Word file, no browser needed. That's different from the Website chapter's `pyodide-interaktiv` cells, which only run live in a browser (see the Extensions cheatsheet).
:::

**Preview vs. Render** (same idea as for a website, just for one file):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `quarto preview exercises.qmd` | Live browser view, updates on save |
| `quarto render exercises.qmd` | Builds the final output file once |

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 3 — Output formats

One `.qmd` file, several possible outputs — change the `format:` line:

| Format | YAML value | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| HTML | `format: html` | Nothing extra |
| Word | `format: docx` | Nothing extra |
| PDF | `format: pdf` | TinyTeX (page 1) |

**All formats at once:**

```yaml
---
title: "Exercise Sheet 1"
format:
  html: default
  pdf: default
  docx: default
---
```

Run `quarto render` once — Quarto produces all three files in the same folder.

```{=latex}
\begin{spotlight}{Good to know}
\begin{itemize}
\item Only need one of several configured formats right now? \texttt{quarto render exercises.qmd --to pdf} renders just that one.
\item \texttt{\{\{< pagebreak >\}\}} on its own line forces a new page --- handy to keep one exercise per printed page.
\item Want your own letterhead or styles in the \texttt{.docx} output? \texttt{format: docx: reference-doc: template.docx} applies a Word template.
\end{itemize}
\end{spotlight}
```
